_comment: The sub-agent roster. Agents are DATA, not code — the same seam financial_data/registry.json draws for providers. Adding a specialist means adding an entry plus a module implementing mas/contract.py; the planner, the executor and the UI change not at all. `writes` is the field to read first: it names every side effect an agent can cause on another service, because a capability that mutates someone else's journal must never be reachable by the same automatic path as a read.

options_pilot.name: OptionsPilot
options_pilot.role: Options specialist, priced from live chains

writes.run_pipeline: freezes ideas into OptionsPilot's own journal on a different service; user-triggered only, never planned automatically

options_pilot.notes: Strictly better than a model when it can answer: real quotes, a real IV surface, and its own forward record. It covers a bounded universe of ~31 names, so 'unavailable' here is the normal case, not a fault.

derivatives.name: Local derivatives engine
derivatives.role: Model pricing for everything OptionsPilot does not cover
derivatives.notes: Black-Scholes / CRR driven by REALIZED volatility. Priority 50 keeps it below OptionsPilot so a real chain always wins where one exists. Reliability 0.55 is not a slight on the arithmetic — it reflects that realized vol is the wrong input for an option price, and is the single largest source of error in anything this agent returns.

cross_asset.name: Cross-asset context
cross_asset.role: How much of this move is just the benchmark?
cross_asset.notes: Each class gets the benchmark it is actually driven by — an altcoin against BTC, an equity against the S&P, a currency against the dollar index. Beta to the WRONG benchmark is the specific error this replaces: yfinance reports a 'beta' for a coin computed against the equity market, which is a number with no meaning that the risk pillar would otherwise consume.
